notes.text: Re-check the output-size formula next time by having the learner contrast the stride-1 case they answered as 32 with the stride-2 case they also answered as 32.
Build on their correct weighted-sum description of convolution to teach stride 2 as computing that sum at every second position.

Next time have the learner compute output sizes with combined padding plus stride greater than 1 including floor cases, since the formula recall and basic stride-1 and stride-2 applications were correct.
Build on the correct 7-pixel receptive field for three 3x3 stride-1 convs by asking for deeper stacks or stride-2 layers next.
Re-check pooling by asking when shift tolerance helps versus hurts localization, since only a single correct recognition of that idea was shown.
Have the learner compute both eigenvectors of [[1,1],[0,2]] and dot them to check they are not orthogonal.
Use the correct Av=lambda v definition and diagonal-matrix success to practice finding eigenvectors of triangular matrices.
Push the correct biggest-eigenvalue-grows-fastest intuition for power iteration to compare growth by |lambda|^k and dependence on the starting vector.
Build on the solid zero-determinant-as-squashing picture to introduce zero eigenvalue with the collapsed direction as its eigenvector.
Re-teach that singular values are not eigenvalues of A by deriving them as square roots of eigenvalues of A^T A starting from the correct U Sigma V^T form.
Confront the non-orthogonality claim by contrasting eigenvectors of the symmetric covariance matrix with general eigenvectors while reaffirming the greatest-variance direction.
Build on the correct squared-singular-value variance calculation to connect SVD to PCA explained variance next time.

links.why: Learner described singular values as the eigenvalues of A.
Learner correctly used squared singular values to compute variance kept by PCs.

notes.text: Have the learner compute 2-3 successive updates for L=w^2 with η=1.1 to see oscillation/divergence and contrast it with their correct single step at η=0.1.
Build on the learner's correct steep-curvature answer to derive the stability limit from curvature 100 and re-apply it to explain why η=1.1 diverges.
Use the learner's correct running-average description of momentum to show how damping zig-zags differs from simply increasing the learning rate.
Have the learner recompute the drone P(drone|fire) from their recalled conditional formula by expanding numerator and denominator with the 1% base rate.
Give a new low-base-rate Bayes problem requiring an explicit total-probability denominator to verify they no longer report sensitivity as the posterior.
Re-teach why MLE variance divides by n and underestimates true variance, building on their correct sample-mean MLE, since the variance item was left unanswered after reveal.
Next time re-check that one homography fits only a single plane by having the learner contrast the tilted pad plane versus the background hill depth.
Build on solid recall of 4 correspondences and perspective-division nonlinearity to derive the 2-equations-per-point DLT setup.
Build on correct selection of the smallest right singular vector to have the learner walk through full Ah=0 estimation next.
Use the correct 128 to 32 double stride-2 calculation as a warm-up anchor before introducing new conv sizing variants.

links.why: Learner applied smallest right singular vector to solve the homography DLT system.
